### Observation specs per entry point (foundations O1, step 1): lib/src/observations.rs, jvmcontract observations, and observe::entry_points

change `lslmmpwrvxuz` · [log `a10f822cf2ed`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/e65240e3-5cf7-41e9-b648-0b36ce9f1129/a10f822cf2eda481d43a923401b4637dd3881e543f78a2a36e681479fb85e107.jsonl.gz)

The observations stream's first step. A new module reads the boundary analysis's facts into the shared IR as one EntryPointSpec per route, message listener, schedule and application-event listener: a stable id (POST /quotes, kafka TOPIC, schedule ARGS, event TYPE), the external inputs with how each is bound (identity derivations: both versions get the same request), the result, exception and a route's status per outcome, one effect observation per modeled call with the payload paths it snapshots at the call, each effect site with its transaction placement, the identity policy, the environment model (every modeled call, outcome 'returns', trace bound 4, exact order, its restriction stated as an assumption) and what the analysis can't see, named (dynamic call sites such as string concatenation, calls it can't follow, computed targets, framework-supplied parameters). reach.rs records each effect's call site for it; the boundary contract's text is unchanged. New command 'jvmcontract observations PATHS [--json]'.

### Observation specs for every Box Office entry point (foundations O1, step 2), with sibling modules followed

change `zmqrplsqzwmm` · [log `278ea47be6bd`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/e65240e3-5cf7-41e9-b648-0b36ce9f1129/278ea47be6bdfa79870dc448cc0bf7b5fc6da19b47f5317a6cbb5f9972ebbd57.jsonl.gz)

jvmcontract observations now gives a spec for each of Box Office's 13 routes, listeners and schedules (ticketing-service 9, payment-service 3, messaging 1). They were checked by hand against the source and the boundary contracts, and that check found three bugs, now fixed. First, the walk didn't enter sibling modules, so the outbox and inbox writes, the placement inside Transactions.run and the guards' 500s were missing. observations::analyse now takes the entry-point classes and the followed classes as two sets, as boundaries::analyse_in does, and the command takes --base DIR, as verify does. Second, a Class argument was expanded into the document's fields as payload; reach.rs now keeps a class literal's declared type. Third, a method inherited from the library (Enum.ordinal) was named unresolved; it is now a library call. The trace bound is now at least the number of effect sites.

### Two builds' observation specs compared into accounted obligations (foundations O2, step 1): observations::compare and observations --against

change `xstwptusvqsx` · [log `fc77552d2be4`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/e65240e3-5cf7-41e9-b648-0b36ce9f1129/fc77552d2be43ed25a2dc85f04f7a4c2cbc07394fe45fa6a93c331c47e9e4264.jsonl.gz)

observe::compare, which returned a named Unsupported since Phase 0, now matches the entry points of two builds by what their consumers address: verb and route with path variable names erased, topic or queue, schedule. A renamed handler is the same entry point. A renamed route is one entry point removed and one new, with the handler that now serves the new route named, because only a person can say the route change is intended. Every observation of every old entry point gets exactly one obligation: preserved (to prove; the shapes agree, which discharges nothing), changed (a status mapping, a payload path, an effect moved into or out of a transaction or to another target, the response type), removed, or unresolved (an unknown status, or entry points a key can't tell apart). Two more obligations sit beside them: 'inputs', for a change to the external inputs, which belong to the preservation contract, and 'unresolved', for what the analysis can't see. Each obligation says what discharging it needs. observations::unaccounted checks that the accounting is complete. New option: jvmcontract observations ... --against OLD.json. Obligation gained new_entry, differences and needs, all with serde defaults.

### Box Office examples 110-119 compared into accounted obligations (foundations O2, step 2): outcomes before the handler, body wire shapes, and what no spec observes

change `yvpqmlqtoqzv` · [log `770eecbafff5`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/e65240e3-5cf7-41e9-b648-0b36ce9f1129/770eecbafff5e07c9891fd4db76e4f23ec3cd67cc9c1a232faa8186739cacabd.jsonl.gz)

Each of Box Office's examples 110-119 is now compared with Box Office as it is, and lib/tests/observations.rs checks the result against what the example's recorded boundary diff says changed at the entry points. The test applies each patch to a copy of the sources, recompiles only the modules the patch changes with javac -parameters, as the Gradle build compiles them, and compares every module's specs with the base build's. Every obligation that is not preserved-to-prove or unresolved has to match a per-example table, along with the differences that say why.

The gaps the examples showed are closed in the spec. Each route's statuses now start with the outcomes the framework takes before the handler runs, and each names the requests it applies to (new field StatusOutcome::when). There are two such outcomes. Bean Validation of a @Valid or @Validated body gives a MethodArgumentNotValidException, answered 400 unless an @ExceptionHandler takes it, for a body that fails one of the constraints it runs. A parameter that can't bind, as binding::check finds it, gives a MissingPathVariableException, a 500 on every request. A body's wire shape, with the wire block's ! lines, is now part of the input domain (new field Binding::shape).

The comparison changed in six ways. An outcome taken before the handler that only one build has, or that applies to other requests, is changed: 110 drops @Valid, and 113 adds a @NotNull billing whose unchecked constraints are named in its inputs obligation. A build that fails every request before the handler changes every observation of that handler (118). A status one build answers for an exception, with no exception of the other answered with it, is changed even when the normal return's status is unknown (119: the 409 is gone). Where an effect attempt is gone, what the new build attempts instead is named (117). A new effect in an existing entry point needs a person's approval or a proof that it is never reached, and the count says how many there are (116, 117). 111, 112 and 114 change no spec at all; what no entry-point spec observes is now printed under every comparison (observations::NOT_OBSERVED). 115 shows up as a changed payload path on an insert.

Two smaller changes. observations --base with a relative path followed no sibling module, because class path entries are absolute; the base is now compared canonically, as verify does. And O1 step 2's two-line addition to examples/apps/boxoffice/README.md is removed again: build.py digests the whole tree into its claim records, so those lines made the recorded results of examples 006, 012, 110 and 111 look stale, and lib/README.md already says the same thing. Each example's notes now say what its comparison gives, and the pages are re-rendered.

Verified: the full cargo test passes (183 unit, 64 integration, 9 conformance with 2 ignored, 3 foundations, 12 observations). rustfmt and clippy are not installed here, so neither was run. Brief Progress: O2 is done; next is O3's narrow case for the joint example.

### The joint example's effect obligation discharged by an effect trace (foundations O3, narrow case): recording stubs, one environment model, a proof of the refactor, and the dropped and duplicated events refuted with witnesses replayed on a JVM

change `kxkxxrovypzs` · [log `83e2f9e1a407`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/e65240e3-5cf7-41e9-b648-0b36ce9f1129/83e2f9e1a407c755079ca729dfb4fc0f30e04d8f9d80b23fd54e9e454d83d400.jsonl.gz)

New module lib/src/effects.rs, behind observe::effect_log and observe::check of the foundations IR. In both builds alike, every call site of a modeled boundary call is redirected to a generated recording stub (with shared::redirect_calls, called unchanged). A stub of an observed effect appends one attempt to a log, with its payload paths snapshotted at the call: a string as the literal of either build it is, a record component through its accessor. One environment model serves both builds; every modeled call returns normally, stated as an assumption. A generated method in the handler's package makes the handler with its one constructor and null dependencies, calls it on the entry point's inputs, and returns the log: the outcome by exception class, the response, and the attempts in exact order. The existing regression harness proves the two logs equal, as a new caller of equivalence::run with the own checker. An attempt past the trace bound, a string that is no literal, a call on a dependency the model doesn't have, or a NullPointerException out of the handler marks the log unresolved, differently in each build. So no proof covers such an input, and a witness on it is reported unresolved, never as a shorter trace. A counterexample is replayed on a JVM under the stubs (jvm_witness::run) and decoded into what each build attempted. Refused by name: a handler that uses a modeled call's result, non-integral inputs or response, an application object among the dependencies, and failure outcomes in the model.

Verified inline (each proof takes under a second). The refactor is verified, with result, exception, status and the Kafka send preserved. dropped-effect is refuted at cents=1, quantity=100: the old build sends total=90 and the new one nothing. duplicated-effect is refuted at quantity=10: one send against the same send twice. offset is refuted at cents=0, quantity=1. Each witness was replayed on JDK 25. The duplicate under trace bound 1 is unresolved, and POST /quotes/text is unresolved. The integration contract's observations part now passes whole: 13 passed, 0 failed, and only the heap, alignment and summaries parts are still unsupported. New tests: lib/tests/effects.rs (10). The full cargo test passes: 183 unit, 64 integration, 9 conformance, 12 observations, 3 foundations, 10 effects. rustfmt and clippy aren't installed here, so neither was run.

Also fixed: the Box Office patch test in lib/tests/observations.rs compiled the patched modules without -g, unlike Gradle. reach.rs reads a local's type from the local variable table, so the new per-site argument classes differed (Update against UpdateDefinition); the test now passes -g. observe.rs gained EffectSite::arguments (CallArgument), and EffectLogPlan::stubs and assumptions (RecordingStub), all with serde defaults. Shared files touched, by adding: lib/src/lib.rs, lib/tests/effects.rs (new), lib/tests/observations.rs and lib/README.md. The brief's Progress records this step and the next one (the rest of O3, from examples 170-179).

### The effect check from the command line (foundations O3, the rest, step 1): jvmcontract effects checks every entry point of two builds under the claim its own spec makes

change `upkxnrotoxsk` · [log `d8486d45655b`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/e65240e3-5cf7-41e9-b648-0b36ce9f1129/d8486d45655bcf67dc9afe833488a4b9255314d6516c31c8c8b2cb5f4d00dbbc.jsonl.gz)

New command jvmcontract effects BEFORE AFTER [--entry ID]... [--trace-bound N] [--unwind N] [--max-array-length N] [--json]. Each entry point of the old build's classes is matched to its counterpart in the new build as observations --against matches them, and checked by the effect trace of foundations O3 under the claim its own observation spec makes (effects::claim_for: its inputs, every observation as required, its environment model, no change approved). It prints, per entry point, the verdict, what each required observation became, the replayed witness with both builds' attempts or why the result is unresolved, the proof line, the domain and the assumptions, then the count. An entry point with no counterpart is unresolved; one the narrow case refuses is reported as unsupported while the rest are still checked. Exit 0 only when every entry point checked is verified.

On the joint example (lib/tests/fixtures/foundations): before against after verifies POST /quotes and leaves POST /quotes/text unresolved (string concatenation); against dropped-effect and duplicated-effect it refutes POST /quotes with witnesses replayed on JDK 25 under the recording stubs. ### A Crosscut kernel behind a thin route, refactored and proved, a dropped and a duplicated send refuted (foundations O3, the rest, step 2; examples 170-172) (verification pending)

change `uqzznykpolmp` · [log `eea1a0e06499`](https://terminalvalue.net/raw-traces/e65240e3-5cf7-41e9-b648-0b36ce9f1129/eea1a0e064993e146791f69a6de002586d28a1fd04e4556a52a78c0f3ba56790.jsonl.gz)

New app examples/apps/deliveries: POST /deliveries/failures asks Crosscut's RetryPolicy whether a failed webhook delivery is retried, and sends a RetryScheduled or a DeadLettered record through a KafkaTemplate. It compiles with Crosscut's kernels against Spring stand-ins kept off the checked build, with plain tests. Box Office and Crosscut are untouched, so no recorded result goes stale. The three examples share one refactor: RetryPolicy.shouldRetry rewritten over two helpers, and the route reorganised around the policy's answer. Example 170 is that refactor, which jvmcontract effects verifies (answer, status and the ordered trace of sends preserved for every int status, boolean idempotency and int attempt count). Example 171 adds a shortcut that answers 200 for a client error without the dead letter; it is refuted at status=400, idempotent=false, attempts=0. Example 172 adds an early dead letter without a return; it is refuted at attempts=5, with one dead letter against two. Every check ran inline in under half a second, the witnesses were replayed on JDK 25.0.5, and the app's tests pass in all three.

To support the route, the recording stubs now handle a modeled call whose sites pass payloads of several classes, which the narrow case refused. Each payload path is read through the payload's own class, a path that class lacks is snapshotted as absent, and the class itself is snapshotted as data.class, so payloads of two classes never compare equal. jvmcontract effects gained --report DIR (effects.sarif, rule effects-changed) with --sources and --base. A boolean witness input now prints as true or false. build.py gained TOOL_APPS['deliveries'] (with stubs and uses), a run_tool_effects B9 runner, effect-specific page text, and bound-only proof options for it. All of this is additive. There is a new technique tag, effect-trace.

**What it does**
- **Matching entry points.** Two builds' entry points are paired by what callers address: method and route (with path variable names ignored), topic or queue, or schedule.
  - A handler that is only renamed is still the same entry point.
  - A renamed route counts as one entry point removed and one added, and the result names the handler that now serves the new route. Only a person can say the rename was intended.
- **One obligation per old observation.** Each observation of each old entry point gets exactly one obligation, so none can drop out of the count. A check confirms nothing is left uncounted. The obligation says one of:
  - **preserved, to prove:** the two specs have the same shape, which proves nothing yet;
  - **changed:** a status mapping, a payload field, an effect moved into or out of a transaction or to another target, or the response type;
  - **removed;**
  - **unresolved:** an unknown status, or entry points the matching can't tell apart.

I finished O3's narrow case: the joint example's effect obligation is now discharged, which completes this stream's core (O1, O2, and O3's narrow case). It's committed as `kxkxxrov`; nothing was submitted as a job, since each proof takes under a second.

**How it works** (new module `lib/src/effects.rs`, behind `observe::effect_log` and `observe::check`):
- **Recording stubs.** In both builds, every call to a modeled boundary method (here `KafkaTemplate.send`) is replaced by a stub. The stub logs the attempt with its payload values copied at the moment of the call.
- **One environment.** The same model serves both builds, and every modeled call returns normally; the result states that as an assumption.
- **The check.** A generated method makes the controller with null dependencies, calls the handler, and returns a log of the outcome, the response and the attempts in exact order. The existing regression harness then proves the two builds' logs equal.
- **Bounds stay visible.** Anything the stubs can't stand behind leaves the result unresolved: going past the trace bound, a string that isn't a literal in either build, an unmodeled call on a dependency, or a `NullPointerException` out of the handler. It is never reported as a shorter trace.
- **Replay.** Each counterexample is re-run on a real JVM with the stubs in place, and the witness says it was not run against real infrastructure.

I added a `jvmcontract effects` command and committed it (`upkxnrot`, `6d21d181428f`). It runs the effect check over two builds from the command line, which was the first step of the rest of O3.

- **What it does:** it takes the old and new builds' class directories and pairs each entry point with its counterpart, the same way `observations --against` does. Each pair is checked against what the old entry point's own spec says must be preserved, with no change approved. Options are `--entry`, `--trace-bound`, `--unwind`, `--max-array-length` and `--json`.
- **Output and exit code:** for each entry point it prints:
  - the verdict, and what became of each required observation;
  - the proof line, or the witness replayed on the JVM with what each build attempted;
  - why a result is unresolved, if it is;
  - the domain and the assumptions.

  It exits 0 only when every entry point checked is verified. An entry point the narrow case can't handle is reported as unsupported, and the rest are still checked.
- **On the joint example:**
  - against the correct refactor, `POST /quotes` is verified and `POST /quotes/text` stays unresolved;
  - with the event dropped, `POST /quotes` is refuted at cents=1, quantity=100;
  - with the event duplicated, it is refuted at cents=1, quantity=10.

  Both witnesses were replayed on JDK 25.
